title: Rust seq_is_newer retains bflq-class naming inversion: LOLLIPOP_CIRCULAR_BIT=128 and both-circular branch commented 'Linear region'
description: Sibling residual of b7z9.88.1 verification round; bflq's deliverable (C rename LOLLIPOP_CIRCULAR_BIT->LOLLIPOP_LINEAR_BASE + RFC-correct region comments in lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/dodag.c) is DONE at HEAD — but the Rust port kept the old shape: rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs:61 'const LOLLIPOP_CIRCULAR_BIT: u8 = 128' and routing.rs:71-72 comments 'Linear region' on the (true,true) branch, where (true,true) means BOTH seqs < 128 — the RFC 6550 §7.2 CIRCULAR region (RFC: [128..255] linear, [0..127] circular). Behavior verified correct (region-agnostic same-region window arithmetic matches C dodag.c lollipop_is_newer and the golden sweep); the hazard is the same as bflq's: a maintainer 'fixing' the comment or constant to RFC region names breaks interop. Fix: rename LOLLIPOP_CIRCULAR_BIT->LOLLIPOP_LINEAR_BASE (or REGION_SPLIT), correct routing.rs:71+ region comments, leave seq_is_newer arithmetic and the rpl_dao_sequence golden sweep untouched (tests/rpl_dao_sequence/gen_golden_sweep.py:25-30 documents the cross-impl constant mapping — update its comment to the new name). Also mirror-check python lollipop comments if they carry the same inversion. Verify: cargo test -p lichen-rpl (std feature), rpl_dao_sequence host suite still green.
